description: The two SHARED-PACKAGE fixes that land in wecare-whatsapp-business-api: F-4 (one Cognito-subject predicate in lambda_utils/customer_auth.py applied across SEVEN identity-filter sites, so the literal UUID regex appears exactly once in the tree) and F-6 (list_orders stops offering an internal order UUID as a customer-facing label, returns a PLAIN LIST, and its accidental second job as an eligibility gate moves to a new has_prior_order). Grouped because both are shared-package changes subject to the SAME binding ordering constraint - they must land AFTER FEAT-001's single-function F-1 commit, never before, or a fleet-wide publisher would sweep F-1's target - and because both edit flows/paid_submit_request.py and flows/catalog_services.py, so splitting them would mean two coders touching the same two files. Two commits, one per F-item, F-4 first (F-6's call-site edit in catalog_services.py sits two lines from F-4's guard there). Corresponds to plan.md Part A items 5 and 6. The DEPLOY is OWNER CONFIRM (O10) AND blocked on O11 AND blocked on the v89-vs-source certification, plan.md Part B rows B3/B4 - do not deploy.
steps: STEP 0 - read context.json and this file FIRST, then plan.md Part A items 5 and 6. Re-derive every anchor on the merged tree; FEAT-001's findings win over plan.md's numbers where they differ.

F-4 STEP 1 - re-derive the seven sites with `git grep -n "Filter='sub" -- amplify` (expect SEVEN; if you see six, FEAT-001's merge did not land and you must stop) and the two inline guards with `git grep -n 're.fullmatch' -- amplify/functions/messaging/whatsapp-business-api/flows/customer_commands.py amplify/functions/messaging/whatsapp-business-api/flows/customer_orders.py` (expect customer_commands.py:80 and customer_orders.py:57). Confirm the helper is still absent: `git grep -n 'is_cognito_subject' -- amplify` returns nothing.

F-4 STEP 2 - add ONE definition to amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/customer_auth.py: `def is_cognito_subject(value) -> bool` returning a FULL match of r'[0-9a-f]{8}(?:-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}' - the SAME pattern the two inline guards use, so there is NO behaviour change on well-formed input. Add `import re` (the module currently imports json, logging, os at :39-41 and has no re). Add "is_cognito_subject" to __all__ at :280-292. Docstring: a Cognito sub is a canonical lowercase UUID; refuse malformed filter inputs before ListUsers. This module is the right home - it already owns CUSTOMER_POOL_ID (:48), CustomerNotAuthorized (:72) and customer_id_from_attributes (:136), and all seven sites already import it to read CUSTOMER_POOL_ID.

F-4 STEP 3 - CONVERT the two already-guarded sites so the literal regex stops being duplicated. flows/customer_commands.py:80: replace the inline re.fullmatch with customer_auth.is_cognito_subject(owner); it KEEPS returning {'outcome': 'VERIFIED_CUSTOMER_REQUIRED', 'reply': <the existing sign-in text>}. flows/customer_orders.py:57: replace the inline re.fullmatch with the helper; it KEEPS RAISING customer_auth.CustomerNotAuthorized('account unavailable'). The two sites differ in refusal MECHANISM (return vs raise) and that difference is PRESERVED - only the predicate is shared. `re` must stay imported in customer_orders.py: TOKEN_PATTERN at :16 still uses it. In customer_commands.py `re` also stays - :22 uses re.fullmatch for the 'orders page N' command.

F-4 STEP 4 - GUARD the five unguarded sites so each refuses BEFORE calling list_users, each keeping the refusal its own call site already returns. (a) flows/catalog_services.py:50 - WIDEN the existing `if not owner:` to `if not customer_auth.is_cognito_subject(owner):`, which guards the list_users at :55; the existing _send(...) + `return {'outcome': 'VERIFIED_CUSTOMER_REQUIRED'}` body is unchanged. (b) ecommerce/checkout/handler.py:3076-3077 - WIDEN `if not owner or owner != row.get('customerId'):` to `if not customer_auth.is_cognito_subject(owner) or owner != row.get('customerId'):`, which guards :3080; the `return {'outcome': 'VERIFIED_CUSTOMER_REQUIRED'}` at :3078 is unchanged. Widening the existing truthiness guards rather than adding a second `if` is the smallest change that covers all four malformed inputs with the SAME refusal the site already returns, and keeps the number of refusal paths unchanged. (c) flows/paid_submit_request.py, immediately before the list_users at :90, insert `if not customer_auth.is_cognito_subject(row['customerId']): return {'outcome': 'VERIFIED_RECIPIENT_UNAVAILABLE'}`. (d) the same insertion immediately before the second list_users at :142. (e) the same insertion in flows/paid_vault.py immediately before the list_users at :69.

F-4 STEP 5 - write tests/test_customer_identity_filter_guard.py. Parametrise over the FIVE previously-unguarded sites with a cognito-idp double that RAISES on any call. Feed four malformed inputs: '" or sub = "x', '', 'not-a-uuid', and an UPPERCASE UUID. Assert each site returns its verified-customer refusal - VERIFIED_CUSTOMER_REQUIRED for catalog_services and checkout, VERIFIED_RECIPIENT_UNAVAILABLE for the three flow sites - with the client NEVER INVOKED. All five fail today. Then add the TWO PIN CASES, which must pass BEFORE AND AFTER so the conversion cannot silently change a working refusal: test_customer_commands_still_refuses_a_malformed_subject (returns {'outcome': 'VERIFIED_CUSTOMER_REQUIRED'} with the sign-in reply, double never invoked) and test_customer_orders_still_refuses_a_malformed_subject (RAISES customer_auth.CustomerNotAuthorized, double never invoked). Seven sites, seven assertions, one regex.

F-4 STEP 6 - confirm the invariant the fix exists for: `git grep -c '0-9a-f]{8}(?:-' -- amplify` must find the literal EXACTLY ONCE, in customer_auth.py. Then run the new file, then the owning suites (tests/test_customer_orders_flow.py, tests/test_paid_vault.py, tests/test_paid_submit_request.py, and whatever `ls tests | grep -E 'customer_auth|checkout'` reports), then the whole suite. Commit F-4 with its test, staging exact paths only: the seven source files plus customer_auth.py plus tests/test_customer_identity_filter_guard.py.

F-6 STEP 1 - re-derive: `git grep -n "orderNumber') or oid" -- amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/paid_submit_request.py` (:96), `git grep -n '^def list_orders' -- <same>` (:80), and `git grep -n 'list_orders' -- amplify/functions/messaging/whatsapp-business-api/flows/catalog_services.py` (:64 import, :65 call).

F-6 STEP 2 - DECISION 1 IS BINDING: the return value stays list[dict]. The skipped count is LOGGED, NEVER RETURNED. A 2-tuple is always truthy, which would make flows/paid_submit_request.py:33's `if not choices:` never fire, the NO_ORDERS screen at :34 unreachable, and would serialise a tuple into a LIVE Flow screen. DECISION 2 IS BINDING: the display rule is applied INSIDE list_orders' loop, where both orderNumber and oid are already in scope at :96 - not in a separate pass over its output, which cannot work because :96 collapses the two into one `title`.

F-6 STEP 3 - in amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/paid_submit_request.py replace :96-97 with: `label = current.get('orderNumber')` / `if not order_keys.is_public_order_number(label):` / a two-line comment recording that the display rule is a public order number or nothing, never an internal UUID, and that flows/customer_commands.order_page already refuses exactly this / `skipped += 1` / `continue` / then `result.append({'id': oid, 'title': str(label)[:60]})`. Initialise `skipped = 0` beside `result = []` at :86. After the loop and before the `return` at :104 add `if skipped: log_event(logger, 'order_choices_unnumbered', skipped=skipped)`.

F-6 STEP 4 - use order_keys.is_public_order_number (order_keys.py:222), NOT is_current_public_order_number (:238). The former deliberately accepts BOTH the current WD-ORD-XXXXXXXX form and the bare 12-character legacy form - its docstring rationale at :223-231 is that refusing a historical number would break every order placed before the change. The stricter predicate would silently drop every pre-prefix order. list_orders keeps its name, signature, dict shape and ownership semantics; DO NOT add a third key to the returned dicts - that payload is serialised into a live Flow screen and a shape change there is a larger blast radius than the defect.

F-6 STEP 5 - the logging imports: TWO are needed. The module imports only hashlib (:8), hmac (:9), secrets (:10), time (:11), typing.Any (:12) and `order_keys, service_request_store as store` (:13) - it has no logger and no json. Add `from lambda_utils.logging import get_logger, log_event` beside the :13 import and `logger = get_logger(__name__)` at module scope. Use log_event (logging.py:28, signature (logger, event_name, level='info', **kwargs)) rather than a hand-rolled json.dumps - it emits the structured JSON itself, so the json import is not needed at all. get_logger (:17) is import-safe here: it creates no client and reads no secret, which matters because this module is imported on the paid path. THE COUNT IS THE ONLY FIELD - never a fileId, orderId, phone or filename.

F-6 STEP 6 - add has_prior_order beside list_orders. THIS IS THE PART THAT MUST NOT BE GOT WRONG: list_orders' return value also serves as a boolean eligibility gate at flows/catalog_services.py:64-70, so narrowing list_orders without this would flip a customer whose prior orders are all legacy from ELIGIBLE TO REFUSED - a purchase-blocking behaviour change on the gated native path where it is hardest to notice. Signature `def has_prior_order(orders: Any, row: dict) -> bool` with the docstring from plan.md item 6 verbatim (eligibility only; deliberately does NOT apply the display rule; a legacy-only customer is still entitled to buy Submit Request and simply sees a shorter selector; keeping these two questions in one function is what made the naive version purchase-blocking). Implement as the same customerId=:owner query with the same ConsistentRead=True ownership recheck and the same `oid == row['orderId']` self-exclusion, short-circuiting True on the first qualifying row.

F-6 STEP 7 - switch the call site: flows/catalog_services.py:64 imports has_prior_order, and :65 becomes `if not has_prior_order(...)`. Two lines. The _send body and the `return {'outcome': 'SUBMIT_REQUEST_PARENT_ORDER_REQUIRED'}` are unchanged.

F-6 STEP 8 - write tests/test_paid_submit_request_order_labels.py, six cases. (1) test_orders_without_a_public_number_are_not_offered - one orderNumber-bearing row and one without; list_orders has length 1 and no returned title matches the UUID regex. Fails today: both offered, one with a UUID title. (2) test_list_orders_returns_a_plain_list - isinstance(result, list), and an input whose rows ALL lack orderNumber yields [] so flows/paid_submit_request.py:34's NO_ORDERS screen actually fires. This is the test that catches the tuple mistake. (3) test_a_legacy_only_customer_is_still_eligible - a fake table whose only rows lack orderNumber; has_prior_order(...) is True so catalog_services.py:65 does NOT emit SUBMIT_REQUEST_PARENT_ORDER_REQUIRED, WHILE list_orders(...) returns []. Both halves of the separation asserted together; this is the test that would have caught the naive version. (4) test_a_legacy_bare_twelve_character_number_is_still_offered - a pre-prefix bare 12-character orderNumber IS offered. Pins is_public_order_number over is_current_public_order_number. (5) test_the_skipped_count_is_logged_without_identifiers - one numbered and two unnumbered rows; the order_choices_unnumbered record has skipped == 2 and NO value in it contains any orderId from the fixture. Pins the PII posture. (6) test_the_parent_order_is_still_excluded - row['orderId'] present among the queried rows, absent from the result. Sensitivity proof that the new `continue` did not disturb the existing self-exclusion at :91-92.

F-6 STEP 9 - run the new file (see 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 fail, then pass), then tests/test_paid_submit_request.py tests/test_paid_vault.py tests/test_service_lines_dropdocs_vault.py (the NO_ORDERS and selector paths), then the whole suite. Commit F-6 with its test, staging exact paths only: amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/paid_submit_request.py, amplify/functions/messaging/whatsapp-business-api/flows/catalog_services.py, tests/test_paid_submit_request_order_labels.py.

FINAL STEP - set this FEAT's status to completed and record in findings: the whole-suite count after each commit, both commit SHAs, confirmation that the UUID literal now appears exactly once in amplify/, and a note that flows/paid_vault.py has received F-4's guard so FEAT-004 must not duplicate it.

NOTHING PUSHED, no deploy, no Lambda version published, no alias moved, no production Lambda invoked, no feature flag opened, no live WhatsApp send, no AWS call of any kind, no secret read, no record deleted.

=== 1. THE COMMIT SHAs AND THE WHOLE-SUITE COUNT AFTER EACH ===
d2d2f869 - 'test: seed order numbers and Cognito subjects that production could actually mint'. 3 files, +18/-6. Whole suite AFTER: 1 failed, 10469 passed, 6 skipped, 3 xfailed. Measured with production code UNCHANGED (the F-4/F-6 edits were held out of the tree for this run), which is the proof that this commit altered no behaviour: 10469 is EXACTLY the FEAT-002 baseline.
24b6d2ec - F-4, 'fix: one Cognito-subject predicate for all seven ListUsers filter sites'. 8 files, +337/-4. Whole suite AFTER: 1 failed, 10495 passed, 6 skipped, 3 xfailed in 109.65s.
f96fca87 - F-6, 'fix: offer only public order numbers, and ask eligibility as its own question'. 3 files, +275/-5. Whole suite AFTER: 1 failed, 10502 passed, 6 skipped, 3 xfailed in 129.69s.
The gate FEAT-002 set was `passed >= 10469 with the ONE inherited failure and no other`. All three runs meet it, strictly rising, and the only failure in any of them is the inherited tests/test_github_oidc_trust_policy.py::test_fixer_covers_every_oidc_role_the_repository_declares (the GitHubActions-wecare-digital-payment-deploy-temp-20261009 OIDC role that arrived with upstream 4ee4c498 and is unregistered at origin/stack too). Before the change it returned two (flows/customer_commands.py:80 and flows/customer_orders.py:57). BOTH inline regexes were converted, not one - converting only customer_commands, as an earlier design revision specified, would have left two copies and left the stated goal unmet. The invariant is also pinned BY A TEST rather than only by grep: test_the_uuid_pattern_appears_in_exactly_one_file walks amplify/**/*.py and asserts the holder list equals exactly [customer_auth.py].

F-4's only edit to that file was the three-line guard before the ListUsers at :69; it added no import. So FEAT-004 must ADD `from lambda_utils.logging import get_logger, log_event` (and a module-scope logger) itself and will NOT be duplicating anything. The import WAS added in this FEAT to amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/paid_submit_request.py (:14) - a DIFFERENT file, under shared/, do not confuse the two.

=== 4. F-4's SEVEN SITES, ALL GUARDED, EACH KEEPING ITS OWN REFUSAL ===
Re-derived on the merged tree before editing: `git grep -n "Filter='sub" -- amplify` returned SEVEN across SIX files, confirming FEAT-001's merge landed (six would have meant it had not). Final state by grep:
  checkout/handler.py:3074 - existing `if not owner or owner != row.get('customerId')` WIDENED to `if not customer_auth.is_cognito_subject(owner) or owner != row.get('customerId')`. Returns VERIFIED_CUSTOMER_REQUIRED, unchanged. NOTE the drift FEAT-001 recorded held: the guard was at :3073 and the Filter at :3076, not plan.md's :3076-3077/:3080.
  flows/catalog_services.py:50 - existing `if not owner:` WIDENED. _send body + VERIFIED_CUSTOMER_REQUIRED unchanged. FEAT-001's :49 was right, not plan.md's :50.

The return-vs-raise difference between the two converted sites is PRESERVED and is pinned by the two mandated pin tests. `re` remains imported in both converted files (customer_orders' TOKEN_PATTERN at :16, customer_commands' 'orders page N' command at :22). customer_auth.py gained `import re`, the predicate, and "is_cognito_subject" in __all__.
Beyond the mandated seven assertions, test_every_list_users_filter_site_is_guarded scans the tree and asserts the count is SEVEN and that every block building a filter also calls is_cognito_subject first - so an EIGHTH site added later fails. A call site is defined as a block containing BOTH "Filter='sub" and 'list_users(' because customer_auth quotes the filter expression in prose; documentation is not a call site.
tests/test_customer_identity_filter_guard.py: 25 passed. FAILING-FIRST OBSERVED: 21 failed / 4 passed against unmodified source. The four passes are correct - the two pin cases, plus the empty-string input at catalog_services and checkout whose existing truthiness guards already covered it.

=== 5. F-6: PLAIN LIST, RULE INSIDE THE LOOP, COUNT LOGGED, ELIGIBILITY SPLIT OUT ===
list_orders returns list[dict] and the count is LOGGED, never returned - pinned by test_list_orders_returns_a_plain_list, which checks `type(result) is list` AND THEN drives the real Flow router (flow_module.route('INIT',...)) to NO_ORDERS once the only numbered order loses its number. A 2-tuple passes a type-free check and is always truthy, so driving the caller is what actually catches it.
The rule is applied INSIDE the loop at the former :96, where orderNumber and oid are both in scope, using order_keys.is_public_order_number (NOT is_current_public_order_number - test_a_legacy_bare_twelve_character_number_is_still_offered asserts a bare 12-character number passes the loose predicate and FAILS the strict one, so a later tightening breaks the test rather than the customer). `skipped = 0` beside `result = []`; `if skipped: log_event(logger, 'order_choices_unnumbered', skipped=skipped)` after the loop, before the return. NO THIRD KEY was added - the appended dict is still exactly {'id', 'title'}, verified by grep, because that payload is serialised into a live Flow screen.
has_prior_order added beside list_orders with the plan's docstring, implemented as the same customerId=:owner query, the same ConsistentRead=True ownership recheck and the same `oid == row['orderId']` self-exclusion, short-circuiting True on the first qualifying row. flows/catalog_services.py:65-66 now imports and calls it; `git grep list_orders -- flows/` shows the only remaining reference is flows/paid_submit_request.py:32, the legitimate selector caller. _send body and SUBMIT_REQUEST_PARENT_ORDER_REQUIRED unchanged.
test_a_legacy_only_customer_is_still_eligible asserts BOTH halves together (has_prior_order True while list_orders is []), then asserts has_prior_order is False for a stranger's rows, for the purchase's own row, and for an empty table, and then DRIVES flows/catalog_services.handle to prove the call site no longer emits SUBMIT_REQUEST_PARENT_ORDER_REQUIRED and no longer sends the 'could not find an earlier order' copy. That is the purchase-blocking regression, asserted at the call site where it would actually have happened.
test_the_skipped_count_is_logged_without_identifiers asserts skipped == 2, `set(record) == {'event','skipped'}`, and that the rendered record contains none of the fixture's orderIds, the parent orderId, the customer UUID or the phone; it also asserts NO record is emitted when nothing was skipped.
tests/test_paid_submit_request_order_labels.py: 6 passed. FAILING-FIRST OBSERVED: 4 failed / 2 passed. The two passes are honest - the legacy-number and self-exclusion cases are pins meant to hold on both sides of the change, not defect demonstrations. (plan.md predicted five would fail; case 4 passes today because the old fallback offered the legacy row anyway. Recorded rather than forced.)

=== 6. THE ONE DEVIATION FROM THIS FEAT'S ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, OWNER-AUTHORISED IN ADVANCE ===
Acceptance criterion 9 ('every pre-existing test in tests/test_paid_submit_request.py ... still passes UNCHANGED') COULD NOT BE MET, and the build loop STOPPED and asked rather than editing a protected test quietly. THREE pre-existing test fixtures seeded values production can never produce, so the new validators correctly rejected them: 'owner' as a Cognito sub in tests/test_native_catalog_orchestration.py (a sub is a canonical lowercase UUID), and order numbers 'WD-ORD-OLD' in tests/test_paid_submit_request.py and 'WD-ORD-'+kind in tests/test_central_order_directory.py (the minter emits WD-ORD- plus exactly 8 characters of PUBLIC_ORDER_NUMBER_ALPHABET 23456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ; 'OLD' is 3 characters and 'O' is not in the alphabet).
Option A (correct the fixtures) was APPROVED. Option B (weaken the predicate away from is_public_order_number / accept any non-empty subject) and option C (defer F-6) were REJECTED ON THE RECORD - B is the 'never weaken validation to make a test pass' rule and would have left a malformed order number still offered to a customer.
The edits change ONLY seed values and the echo literals that must agree with them. No assertion logic, no control flow, no asserted behaviour. They were committed FIRST and SEPARATELY (d2d2f869), and that commit is GREEN AGAINST UNCHANGED PRODUCTION CODE at exactly the FEAT-002 baseline of 10469 - which is the evidence that it is fixture-only. tests/test_native_catalog_orchestration.py and tests/test_central_order_directory.py sit outside this FEAT's declared file list and were touched for this fixture-realism reason ONLY, as a direct consequence of the restrictions this FEAT introduces - not as unrelated repairs, which plan.md 0.3 forbids. === 8. METHOD NOTES FOR LATER FEATs ===

Used three times here, including to hold F-6 out of the tree so the F-4 whole-suite number is attributable to F-4 alone. No stash, no reset --hard, no clean -f, no rebase.
